# Level Selection System - Setup Guide
## Architecture Overview
This system uses a **data-driven approach** with three main components:
### 1. **LevelData** (Data Model) - `LevelId`: Unique identifier - `LevelNumber`: Display number (1, 2, 3...) - `State`: Current state (Locked, Unlocked, Completed) - `LevelName`: Name of the level - `Difficulty`: Difficulty rating - `HighScore`: Best score achieved
**Why separate from database?** - Runtime data can be modified without affecting the original source - Easy to serialize/deserialize to JSON or binary - Portable between game scenes
### 2. **LevelManager** (Singleton) - Holds all level data - Loads from database/JSON/hardcoded defaults - Provides methods to query and update levels - Persists across scenes (DontDestroyOnLoad)
### 3. **LevelSelection** (UI Manager) - Spawns LevelButton prefabs from LevelManager data - Handles horizontal dragging and scrolling - Manages button interactions - Auto-updates when level progression changes
### 4. **LevelButton** (Individual Button) - Displays level number - Updates visuals based on LevelData state - Handles click events - Can be locked/unlocked/completed
---
## Setup Instructions
### Step 1: Create Managers in Scene 1. Create a new GameObject named "Managers" 2. Add the **LevelManager** script as a component 3. In the Inspector, configure initial levels (or use defaults)
### Step 2: Create Level Selection Panel 1. Create a Canvas and UI Panel named "LevelSelectionPanel" 2. Add **LevelSelection** script to this panel 3. Create a child Panel named "LevelButtonContainer" with **Horizontal Layout Group** 4. Assign this container to the `Level Button Container` field in LevelSelection
### Step 3: Create Level Button Prefab 1. Create a UI Button with Image component 2. Add the **LevelButton** script 3. Create a child Text (TextMeshPro) for the level number 4. Assign sprites to the three states (Locked, Unlocked, Completed) 5. Add an Image component for shadow (optional) 6. Drag this prefab to the `Level Button Prefab` field in LevelSelection
### Step 4: Configure Sprites In LevelButton Inspector: - **Level Locked Sprite**: Grayed-out button image - **Level Unlocked Sprite**: Highlighted/bright button - **Level Completed Sprite**: Gold/special appearance - **Level Text**: The TextMeshPro text component showing level number - **Button Image**: The main button image
---
## How to Use
### Load Levels at Startup ```csharp // LevelManager automatically initializes in Awake() // It loads default levels unless you configure them in the Inspector ```
### Update Level Progress (from game script) ```csharp // Complete a level LevelManager.Instance.UpdateLevelState(levelId, LevelButtonState.Completed, playerScore);
// Unlock next level LevelManager.Instance.UpdateLevelState(nextLevelId, LevelButtonState.Unlocked);
// Refresh UI LevelSelection.Instance.RefreshLevelButtons(); ```
### Scroll to a Specific Level ```csharp LevelSelection.Instance.ScrollToLevel(levelId); ```
### Get Level Data ```csharp LevelData level = LevelManager.Instance.GetLevelById(levelId); Debug.Log($"Level {level.levelNumber}: {level.state}"); ```
---
## Dragging Features
- **Left/Right Drag**: Smoothly scroll through levels - **Momentum**: Continues scrolling with deceleration after you release - **Boundaries**: Automatically clamps so you can't scroll beyond edges - **Sensitivity**: Adjust `Drag Sensitivity` to make dragging faster/slower
Configure in LevelSelection Inspector: - `Drag Sensitivity`: 1.5 (increase for more responsive dragging) - `Deceleration Rate`: 0.95 (lower = stops quicker) - `Min Velocity Threshold`: 0.01 (minimum speed to continue scrolling)
---
## Loading from External Data
Replace `InitializeDefaultLevels()` in LevelManager with your data source:
### From JSON: ```csharp private void InitializeDefaultLevels() { string json = Resources.Load<TextAsset>("levels").text; LevelDataContainer container = JsonUtility.FromJson<LevelDataContainer>(json); allLevels = container.levels; } ```
### From Database: ```csharp private void InitializeDefaultLevels() { allLevels = DatabaseManager.LoadAllLevels(); } ```
---
## Events & Callbacks
The system uses: - `LevelButton.OnLevelButtonClicked()` → Calls `LevelSelection.SelectLevel()` - `LevelSelection.RefreshLevelButtons()` → Updates all button visuals
You can extend this by adding UnityEvents or delegates for custom callbacks.
---
## Tips
✅ Keep LevelManager across scenes for persistent progression ✅ Call `RefreshLevelButtons()` after completing a level ✅ Use LevelData for your game logic, not LevelButton state ✅ Add audio/animations in UpdateVisuals() for polish ✅ Consider adding level descriptions in the LevelData model
